## Summary

Telit's press release on the DL750 describes Danlaw as a global company
dedicated to the engineering, manufacturing and testing of embedded
software, electronics and vehicle network communications, and
introduces the DL750, a second-generation OBD-II datalogger that plugs
in without installation and gets its wireless connectivity from
Telit's GE865-QUAD GSM/GPRS module [3]. The IEEE registry lists two
MA-L blocks and one IAB block to Danlaw Inc at 23700 Research Dr.,
Farmington Hills, Michigan [1][2].

A MAC in a Danlaw block is most likely a vehicle telematics device such
as an OBD-II datalogger [3]. Founding year and ownership are not
documented by the sources consulted, nor is MAC randomization or any
advisory. FCC grantee codes and the radios of Danlaw's later products
are not listed: the FCC ID databases refused the session that verified
this entry, and nothing is filled in from memory.
